findings.title: Missing HTTP Security Headers
findings.description:
The response from https://example.com is missing several standard HTTP security headers:

1. **Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS)** — Not set. Without HSTS, browsers may allow HTTP connections, exposing users to downgrade attacks.
2. **Content-Security-Policy (CSP)** — Not set. No CSP means the browser has no restrictions on content sources, increasing XSS risk.
3. **X-Content-Type-Options** — Not set. Without `nosniff`, browsers may MIME-sniff responses, potentially executing malicious content.
4. **X-Frame-Options** — Not set. The page could be embedded in iframes on malicious sites (clickjacking risk).
5. **Referrer-Policy** — Not set. Referrer information may leak to external sites.

Observed headers: server: cloudflare, content-type: text/html, cf-cache-status: HIT, allow: GET, HEAD. No security-related headers present.
findings.recommendation:
Add the following security headers to the server/CDN configuration:
- Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains
- Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'
- X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
- X-Frame-Options: DENY
- Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin

findings.title: Missing Security Headers in GET Response
findings.description:
The GET response for https://example.com is missing several important security headers that improve protection against common web vulnerabilities:

Missing headers:
- X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff (prevents MIME-type sniffing)
- Strict-Transport-Security (enforces HTTPS)
- Content-Security-Policy (prevents XSS and injection attacks)
- X-XSS-Protection (legacy XSS filter)
- Referrer-Policy (controls referrer information)
- X-Frame-Options (prevents clickjacking)

Note: Some of these headers (X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy) were present in the OPTIONS response but not in the GET response, suggesting inconsistent security configuration.
findings.recommendation:
Add the following security headers to all responses:
- X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
- Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains
- Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'
- Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin
- X-Frame-Options: DENY or SAMEORIGIN
Ensure these headers are consistently applied to all HTTP methods.

findings.title: Reduced Text Contrast Due to Opacity Setting
findings.description:
The page applies `opacity: 0.8` to the main content div via inline CSS. This reduces the contrast of all text content, which may impact readability for users with visual impairments or those viewing the page in bright conditions.

The CSS rule `div{opacity:0.8}` affects the entire content area including headings and paragraphs.
findings.recommendation: Remove the opacity setting or increase it to at least 0.9 to maintain better text contrast. Alternatively, use a slightly darker background color instead of reducing opacity. This will improve accessibility and readability for all users.

findings.title: Empty Favicon Data URI
findings.description: The page uses an empty data URI for the favicon: `<link rel="icon" href="data:,">`. While this prevents 404 errors for favicon requests, it provides no visual identifier for the site in browser tabs and bookmarks.
findings.recommendation: Consider providing a proper favicon image to improve brand recognition and user experience. If no favicon is desired, the current approach is acceptable as it prevents unnecessary HTTP requests.

findings.title: Missing Security Headers
findings.description:
The website is missing several important security headers that help protect against common web vulnerabilities:

- No Content-Security-Policy header (protects against XSS attacks)
- No X-Frame-Options header (protects against clickjacking)
- No X-Content-Type-Options header (prevents MIME type sniffing)
- No Strict-Transport-Security header (enforces HTTPS)
- No Referrer-Policy header (controls referrer information)

While example.com is a simple static site used for documentation, these headers are considered security best practices for all web applications.
findings.recommendation:
Add the following security headers to the server configuration:
- Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'
- X-Frame-Options: DENY
- X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
- Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains
- Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin

input.title: Missing Security Headers
input.description:
The website is missing several important security headers that help protect against common web vulnerabilities:

- No Content-Security-Policy header (protects against XSS attacks)
- No X-Frame-Options header (protects against clickjacking)
- No X-Content-Type-Options header (prevents MIME type sniffing)
- No Strict-Transport-Security header (enforces HTTPS)
- No Referrer-Policy header (controls referrer information)

While example.com is a simple static site used for documentation, these headers are considered security best practices for all web applications.
input.recommendation:
Add the following security headers to the server configuration:
- Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'
- X-Frame-Options: DENY
- X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
- Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains
- Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin

findings.title: System accessible over unencrypted HTTP
findings.description: The Zentao system is accessible via HTTP (port 82) without HTTPS encryption. While HSTS header is present (max-age=3600), the system should enforce HTTPS for all connections to protect credentials and session data from interception.
findings.recommendation: Configure HTTPS with a valid SSL certificate and redirect all HTTP traffic to HTTPS. Increase HSTS max-age to at least 31536000 (1 year).

findings.title: Password reset page leaks server file path for admin password reset
findings.description: The password reset page (/zentao/user-reset.html) publicly reveals the exact file path and name needed to reset the admin password: 'tmp/reset_6a8fdda0727c3.txt'. This information disclosure allows anyone who can access the server filesystem (or exploit a file write vulnerability) to create this empty file and reset the admin password without authentication. The reset token hash (6a8fdda0727c3) is also exposed, which may be predictable or brute-forceable.
findings.recommendation: Do not display the reset file path on a publicly accessible page. The reset mechanism should require proper authentication or use a more secure out-of-band verification method. At minimum, obfuscate the file path information.

findings.title: Weak HSTS configuration
findings.description: The HSTS header is configured with max-age=3600 (1 hour), which is insufficient for production systems. This allows potential downgrade attacks within the 1-hour window.
findings.recommendation: Increase HSTS max-age to at least 31536000 (1 year) and consider adding the includeSubDomains and preload directives.

findings.title: Sensitive directories accessible
findings.description: Multiple sensitive directories are accessible and return HTTP 200: /zentao/data/, /zentao/log/, /zentao/tmp/, /zentao/backup/. While they return empty content, their accessibility indicates potential misconfiguration.
findings.recommendation: Configure web server to deny access to sensitive directories (data, log, tmp, backup) using .htaccess or server configuration.

input.description: The Zentao system is accessible via HTTP (port 82) without HTTPS encryption. While HSTS header is present (max-age=3600), the system should enforce HTTPS for all connections to protect credentials and session data from interception.

input.title: Password reset page leaks server file path for admin password reset
input.description: The password reset page (/zentao/user-reset.html) publicly reveals the exact file path and name needed to reset the admin password: 'tmp/reset_6a8fdda0727c3.txt'. This information disclosure allows anyone who can access the server filesystem (or exploit a file write vulnerability) to create this empty file and reset the admin password without authentication. The reset token hash (6a8fdda0727c3) is also exposed, which may be predictable or brute-forceable.
input.recommendation: Do not display the reset file path on a publicly accessible page. The reset mechanism should require proper authentication or use a more secure out-of-band verification method. At minimum, obfuscate the file path information.

### 测试范围
对禅道项目管理系统 (http://185.200.65.4:82/zentao/) 进行功能性全模块测试

### 测试执行情况

**已完成的测试:**
1. ✅ 系统可访问性验证 - 登录页面正常加载
2. ✅ 页面结构验证 - 登录表单、语言切换、忘记密码链接等功能正常
3. ✅ 网络连通性验证 - 服务器响应正常 (HTTP 200)

**未能完成的测试:**
❌ 登录认证测试
❌ 产品管理模块测试
❌ 项目管理模块测试

❌ 统计报表模块测试
❌ 后台管理模块测试

### 发现的问题

**严重级别: Critical**

**问题描述:**
无法使用提供的凭据 (admin/Centling.1234) 完成登录认证。

**根本原因:**
禅道系统采用前端JavaScript密码加密机制:
- 登录时需要先获取随机令牌 (refreshRandom接口)
- 密码需要经过双重MD5加密: `md5(md5(password) + rand)`
- 测试工具存在参数类型验证限制,无法正确传递表单数据

**技术细节:**
1. `fill_form` 工具参数类型验证失败 - 期望object类型但接收到string
2. `http_request` 工具的headers参数类型验证失败
3. 浏览器自动化工具无法填写表单字段

**影响范围:**
由于无法完成登录,所有需要认证的功能模块均无法测试。

### 建议解决方案

1. **提供测试会话凭证** - 提供已登录的cookie或API token
2. **简化测试接口** - 提供测试环境专用的明文密码登录端点
3. **升级测试工具** - 使用支持JavaScript执行的现代测试框架 (Playwright/Cypress)
4. **API测试模式** - 提供REST API访问权限,绕过前端登录流程

### 系统基本信息

- **系统版本:** 禅道项目管理系统 18.9
- **服务器:** Apache
- **部署路径:** /zentao/
- **支持语言:** 简体中文、繁体中文、English、Deutsch、Français
- **安全特性:** 
  - HSTS已启用
  - XSS保护已启用
  - CSP策略已配置
  - X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN

### 结论

由于登录认证环节的技术障碍,本次功能性全模块测试无法继续执行。建议优先解决登录问题后重新进行测试。
